Subject: Implementation checklist & routing policy notes for Arkadia integration

Hi Maria / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — really appreciate the clear breakdown of your latency targets and regulatory needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the eng sync: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goal: ship semantic search + question-answering into clinician UI with p95 generation latency <= 200ms for short prompts (50–150 tokens).
- Data classification: clinical PHI in scope — customer prefers private deployment (VPC) and KMS-backed key control.
- Volumes: steady traffic ~25 qps with 30–40% peak bursts; most traffic originates US-East.

Proposed implementation (high level):
1) Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) in us-east1 behind your VPC peering. KMS integration for keys + audit logs enabled.
2) SDK & Auth: use Redwood SDK with mTLS for control plane + short-lived API tokens for app services. We’ll share a starter snippet (see attached checklists).
3) Model topology / routing: primary candidate = redwood-7b-llama-q4 for low cost + fast decode; configure routing policy that prefers low-latency variants for UI reads and routes to a higher-quality 13B variant for long-form summarization. Fallback chain: 13B -> 7B -> 3B (fastest) depending on capacity and p95 budget.
4) Embeddings & reranker: bulk embed content offline into your vector DB (we recommend Pinecone/FAISS). For query time, run embedding lookup to get top-50, run a lightweight cross-encoder reranker (13B if budget allows) on top-10 to improve precision.
5) Structured output / tool calling: use Redwood function-calling with schema enforcement for actions (e.g., create-case, surface-evidence). Validate JSON schema in the SDK and fallback to text-only responses on schema failures.

Action items / next steps:
- Please share your VPC architecture diagram and any procurement timeline (Tom). (Attached: arkadia-current-arch.pdf)
- Engineering sync: propose Wed 9 Sep 09:00–10:00 ET or Thu 10 Sep 13:00–14:00 ET.
- We’ll circulate a draft routing-policy.yaml and SDK quickstart before the call (attached: routing-policy-example.yaml, redwood-implementation-checklist.pdf).

If any of this is off, call it out — otherwise we’ll lock the agenda for the eng sync around SDK setup, auth, network, and a model-routing demo.

Best,
Naomi Feldman

Thanks Naomi — and hi Maria. A few engineering notes to make the Wed sync productive: 

Network & Auth:
- For Private: we support VPC peering and Private control plane. KMS integration with customer-managed keys is supported; HSM-backed keys are possible via our KMS partner integrations (we’ll surface the options during the call).
- Auth modes: mTLS between your app services and the Redwood edge is recommended; shorter-lived app tokens for downstream services is an alternative. We can provide an example token rotation Lambda if needed.

SDK setup & routing:
- SDK: The SDK has a small wrapper to select models by policy. We recommend a two-layer router:
  * Route by intent (ui_read | long_form | embed)
  * Within intent, route by latency_budget (low | medium | high) and region preference.
- Example policy (high level):
  latency_budget: low
  - prefer: redwood-3b-q4 (p50 30ms)
  - fallback: redwood-7b-q4
  latency_budget: medium
  - prefer: redwood-7b-q4
  - fallback: redwood-13b-int8
  long_form:
  - prefer: redwood-13b-int8

Fallback chains:
- Implement graceful degradation: if preferred model queue latency exceeds 120% of SLO or if queue depth > threshold, route to next model in chain. Also include a token-cost cap per request to avoid runaway bills. Our routing engine supports these predicates out of the box.

Embeddings & reranker:
- We recommend embedding with batch jobs and storing with your vector store. For reranking, use a small cross-encoder tuned on clinical QA for top-10 re-score. If cost is a concern, run faster bi-encoder similarity for top-50 and then a re-ranker for top-10.

Structured output & tool calling:
- Use our JSON schema enforcement. If schema validation fails, SDK returns a structured error and a fallback plain-text summary. We can instrument automatic alerts when function-calls fail at >1% rate.

Attached a sample routing policy file and a short YAML you can review before the sync (routing-policy-example.yaml).

One thing we’ll ask on the call: do you have an internal SLO definition for p95 (e.g., do you prefer end-to-end from app -> model or just inference)? That determines where we place caching and prefetching.

- Rishi
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
